answer: Serial attention mirror. Each identity must publish a continuous stream of timestamped micro-decisions that peers cross-check against observed outcomes; divergence lowers its mirror score. A sybil cluster repeating one source collapses because its members echo the same timing fingerprint. Sustained hourly attention is the cost: an attacker pays roughly 40 hours of genuine monitoring per identity to keep scores above threshold, so 100 identities cost 4,000 hours, and any slip leaves a visible comet tail of correlated errors. Enforcement: below-threshold scores are rate-limited to zero reach.
